newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Berisha says only parliament can end curfew.
newsitem.headline: Berisha says only parliament can end curfew.

text.p: President Sali Berisha, at odds again with Albania's national unity government, refused on Sunday to lift a curfew before next month's elections.

He told Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and Interior Minister Belul Celo only the new parliament would have powers to end the state of emergency declared in March, when investments schemes wiped out the savings of thousands of Albanians and an anti-Berisha revolt tumbled the country into anarchy.

New elections were promised when opposition parties agreed to join a nine-party coalition to tackle the crisis but preparations have been dogged by disputes over how they will be conducted and supervised.

Fino and Celo met Berisha with a government request that he end the state of emergency, including the 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. curfew, so that parties could campaign normally. State television said Berisha refused.
Opposition parties and the president's office could not be immediately reached for comment.
Berisha dissolved parliament in early May, in preparation for the elections to be held at the end of June.
Albania, Europe's poorest nation, vitally needs the election to restore law and order after anger over the collapse of get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes.
Although the situation has calmed, large swathes of the country remain outside government control. More than a million weapons looted during the troubles have fallen into in private hands.
